items.title: Narvin Kimball Interview, 1961-11-25
items.q: when we were with Paul Moyer's group

ctx.x: And one time, uh, I, I made a record. He, uh, a friend of me, of mine told me that he'd once expressed the wish to make a record. So once when I was recording, uh, Bunk Johnson and, uh, this happened to be Wooden Joe's band. Yeah, he made these with Wooden Joe, Nicholas. Uh huh. And, um, uh, Burbank. And we had him just, he didn't even have his trombone. He'd given up trombone. He used Jim Robinson's trombone. A couple of numbers played Careless Love and St. Louis Blues. He was quite deaf. He had trouble first…

That's right, because when, I can remember that was something else that I remember about him. When he was playing the trombone when, uh, we were with Paul Moyer's group, he had one tooth on the side. It was the, the eye, the eye tooth. And he would place it on the side of the eye tooth and would brace his lip for his embouchure. A strong lip. And he played.
Even when he hadn't played for years, he, after ten minutes time, he'd fill the horn.
